slots.title: Japan’s $50B Yen Intervention in One Day
slots.body:
WSJ: Japan used about **$50 billion in one day** to prop up the yen — described as a record for that kind of one-day spending.

The piece ties that campaign to **rare joint action with the U.S.**

Japan’s benchmark index closed **+3.1%** at **59,205.06** after a **+1,770.29** point move.

That rebound follows coverage linking the session to firmer U.S. jobs data from earlier in the week.

How closely do you track yen intervention headlines versus what shows up in U.S. index futures?

slots.title: China Factory Prices 5.7% vs 5.3% Est.
slots.body:
China’s **PPI** (prices at the factory gate) for October: **5.7%**.

Economists in a Reuters poll had **5.3%**.

That’s the highest wholesale inflation print cited in the headline — framed as a **four-year high** for that measure.

The same story notes the **consumer** inflation gauge slowing on the other side of the economy.

No comparable U.S. CPI print is in today’s calendar from this feed; the read is overseas cost pressure, not a U.S. release.

Do you treat China PPI as a lead indicator for global goods prices, or mostly Asia?

slots.title: US cash session — Nov. 8, 2026
slots.body:

The VIX closed at 25.64, down 9.0% from the prior session, with an intraday low of 23.47.

The latest Treasury snapshot in the feed (dated 2026-11-06) showed the 10-year yield at 4.9% and the 2s10s spread at 0.35 percentage points.
